<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## AITER prerequisites

None. The chunk alignment is in the SGLang scheduler. This change does not call an AITER kernel.

## Motivation

With the mamba extra buffer, a hybrid model can only save a state checkpoint at a depth that is both on the radix page grid and a whole number of kernel chunks from the start of the extend. Chunked prefill can cut a request at any length. After one cut that is not chunk-aligned, every later chunk of that request is off the grid, so the request saves no more checkpoints and later turns miss the prefix cache.

## Modifications

- Round a chunked-prefill cut down to the mamba chunk size when the mamba extra buffer is on.
- Leave the last chunk of a request as is, and keep a cut that would round to zero.
- Add the chunk size to the scheduler's truncation alignment, using the LCM with any existing alignment.
- Add unit tests for the rounding and for a request cut into uneven chunks.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions:

| Base | This PR |
|---:|---:|
| 0.941 | 0.938 |

Both runs use the DCP8 server described below.

GSM8K varies by about 0.01 between runs of the same serving code on this setup (0.950 vs 0.942, and 0.951 vs 0.940, for pairs of branches whose serving path is identical), so a difference of that size is noise.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Result: the prefix cache hit rate rises from 68.6% to 79.6%. The ideal for this workload is about 82%: the first prompt in each group and the 1024-token question in every prompt cannot hit. Mean TTFT is 32% lower and median TTFT 58% lower. TPOT does not change.

MI355X x8, `/data/models/Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`, AITER [`yuychang/aiter@b9229988f`](https://github.com/yuychang/aiter/commit/b9229988f) (the bench AITER build; this scheduler change does not depend on an AITER pull request). Server flags follow the cookbook MI355X cell: TP8, `--dcp-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a`, AITER prefill and decode attention, FP8 KV cache, radix cache on. Workload: `sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name generated-shared-prefix`, 32 groups x 8 prompts, 16384-token shared prefix, 1024-token question, 256 output tokens, concurrency 16, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`. The cache was warmed with a different seed and flushed before the measured run. Both sides set `SGLANG_AITER_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0`: on `main`, the 12-head FP8 PS prefill (`_mla_fp8_prefill_attn_ps`) tries to allocate about 1.2 TiB for a cached prefix with DCP8 and runs out of memory. That bug is unrelated to this PR. The 16K prefix and the 8K chunk size make every prompt span several chunks, which is the case this PR changes.

| Metric | Base | This PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 5369 | 3633 | -32.3% |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 4881 | 2043 | -58.1% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 24.23 | 24.23 | -0.0% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 354.5 | 417.3 | +17.7% |
| Prefix cache hit rate | 68.6% | 79.6% |  |

Tests (MI355X): `test_mamba_checkpoint_depth.py` (13 passed).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
